A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same PhyDetEx work. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including matching material relocated between versions.

before.justification: V1 reports original detection experiments, data-design ablations, T2V benchmarking, and VideoPhy results after PhyDetEx-guided DPO.

after.justification: V2 retains those empirical results and adds tuning comparisons, reasoning and attention analyses, and a vanilla-VLM preference-generation control.

M1.justification: The paired-data construction, Qwen2.5-VL-7B LoRA adaptation, language-modeling objective, and PhyDetEx-guided T2V DPO procedure remain unchanged. Full SFT and detector DPO are added comparison methods, not replacements for the proposed method.

E1.justification: Both retain PID and Impossible Videos evaluation, VIDGEN-1M and VidProM data sources, and downstream VideoPhy evaluation. The added diagnostics and failure examples remain within the existing physical-plausibility task coverage.

E2.justification: V2 adds full SFT and DPO tuning comparators in Table S2 and vanilla Qwen2.5-VL-7B-generated preferences as a downstream DPO comparator in Table S7. The main detection and T2V benchmark comparator sets are unchanged.

E3.justification: V2 adds matched-epoch tuning comparisons and Correct-judgment Reasoning Score (CRS), which evaluates explanations only for correct predictions. It also adds the vanilla-VLM preference-generation control. Existing dataset splits, principal metrics, and reported training budgets remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained balanced/paired-data ablation, v2 adds tuning-strategy comparisons, attention maps examining shortcut behavior, conditional reasoning-quality analysis, and a downstream preference-generator control. Expanded failure analysis adds four missed-detection examples and categorizes their physical interactions, substantially broadening the diagnostic evidence.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. CRS introduces a conditional evaluation metric, not uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: V2 adds tuning scores, CRS results, attention findings, and missed-detection examples. Table S7 adds vanilla-DPO results of 35.92 PC and 42.69 SA; the existing PhyDetEx-DPO results remain 37.63 and 43.81. Main benchmark values are unchanged. The LLaVA-OneVision discussion also corrects 'high Acc. Impl.' to 'high Acc. Plaus.', matching Table 1.

T1.justification: V2 Appendix E introduces CRS as a conditional mean of Reasoning Score over correct predictions, a limited new mathematical definition. The paired-content formalization and objective in Equations (1)-(7) remain unchanged, with no new proofs or theoretical guarantees.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same central claims about PID, lightweight VLM adaptation, detecting and explaining physical implausibility, and benchmarking T2V models. Added analyses support these claims without redefining their scope.

C2.justification: V2 adds interpretations concerning pretrained-knowledge disruption under full SFT, DPO data needs, attention localization, and physics-aware preference supervision. It expands failure categories and discusses visual-only limitations and possible audio/object information, while retaining the original explanation of VLM plausibility bias.

D1.justification: The implementation recipes and access information are retained: LoRA hyperparameters, data-generation and filtering models, A800 hardware, API variants, DPO losses and training settings, and project link. The new analyses do not provide substantive additional implementation recipes.

R1.justification: V2 removes four cited works concerning continual visual programming, top-down visual question answering, Timecausality, and TIIF-Bench. The substantive positioning against existing physical-plausibility evaluation approaches remains unchanged.

P1.justification: V2 moves the additional preliminary-investigation discussion from Appendix A into new Section 5.2, inserts a baseline-analysis appendix section, and makes localized wording and terminology corrections. Most of the existing narrative and section sequence are retained.

P2.justification: V2 adopts a substantially different visual template, including a boxed full-width abstract, colored headings, and a single-column appendix. Figure 2 gains a schematic; attention and missed-detection figures and two tables are added. The preliminary-results table moves into the main text, and appendix displays are extensively repositioned.

improvement.justification: The added tuning and vanilla-VLM DPO controls strengthen support for the design choices, while the expanded failure analysis makes applicability limits clearer. These are useful incremental gains over v1. Sparse implementation reporting for the new analyses and limited evidence for their mechanistic interpretations constrain the improvement; the principal method and benchmark outcomes remain unchanged.
